summary.prose: S001 replaces the legacy scratchpad textarea with Milkdown + Crepe in one VS Code custom text-editor pane backed by the real Markdown TextDocument. It provides remembered lock/pencil controls and a selection Send icon that acts only on a click, alongside safe versioned editing, native document lifecycle integration and explicit error/recovery handling. It preserves identity, browse/new/delete and recency behavior. Published APIs support the design, while real Markdown, undo, save/conflict and host qualification remain mandatory build checks.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The daemon-owned private repository-keyed index remains authoritative for link resolution, backlinks and the title/preview list read-model. Client-side scratchpad editing now uses Milkdown + Crepe inside a VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider on the existing .md TextDocument, replacing the host's built-in vscode.markdown.editor. Insrc owns its selection toolbar and lock state without a native-editor extension API dependency. [[c40]] [[c41]] [[c42]]

ownedContracts.name: ScratchpadRef
ownedContracts.purpose: The one cross-cutting note-identity primitive every link-, lifecycle-, and citation-facing story needs: a stable reference to a scratchpad that survives rename/move/archive/restore. Owned at s1 (the Epic's root) because s2 — which depends only on s1, not on s7 where identity is semantically 'about' — also needs it for the k2 tie-break.

boundary.internal: Milkdown + Crepe hosted in one VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider pane is private to s1. It owns rendering/editing, per-pane lock/pencil controls, explicit selection Send popup, versioned transaction/document synchronization, local asset packaging and TextDocument lifecycle integration. It preserves the .md file and sc1 identity, replaces the old textarea/save protocol atomically and retains browse/new/delete/send/list-refresh behavior. Locked mode keeps selection and Send available; a custom tooltip may be needed because default formatting toolbars can hide when read-only. No s8 attachments, s7 metadata persistence, backlinks or search ranking are implemented here.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The chat-menu cap-10 rendering, the list panel's cap-20/3-line-preview/delete UI, and the relevance-ranking algorithm itself (title-first, tie-break via sc1's stableId) are private to s2; sc3 exposes only the read-model shape (title/preview/mtime), not the ranking logic.

Find-in-note's match highlighting, wraparound navigation, and collapsed-section reveal operate entirely on the open editor's live text buffer — no cross-story data or contract is produced or consumed.

The entry-boundary/timestamp Markdown convention, day-grouping, and the Undated bucket are private to how one note's content renders; no story downstream of s4 in the Epic's dependency graph consumes dated-entry structure, so it is not exposed as a shared contract.

The link-target picker UI and the qualified-target Markdown syntax (percent-encoded target segments, versioned, per the HLD's resolved open question) are private to s5; sc2 exposes only the resolved-reference and backlink-query shape s6 consumes, not the authoring UI or syntax.
The backlink view's grouping-by-source-note rendering, on the pad and on file/symbol surfaces, is private UI; no story is downstream of s6 in the Epic's graph, so it exposes no further contract.

The archive/restore state machine, the permanent-delete confirmation flow, and the decision of where stable ID/repo-association/archive-state are actually persisted are private to s7; it extends sc1's bare ScratchpadRef with lifecycle state but does not re-expose that lifecycle representation as a further contract, since s8/s9/s10 only need sc1's identity.

The attach-to-turn picker UI, the removable-preview rendering, and revision-pinning for a queued turn are private to s8; it consumes sc1 to cite the note and exposes no further contract, since only s9 depends on s8 and s9's own need (provenance link) is satisfied by sc1 directly.
The promote-to-draft action's brainstorm/ISSUE routing and idempotent-retry handling are private to s9; no story is downstream of s9 in the Epic's graph.
The tag-filter UI and starter-template catalog are private to s10; it extends sc3's list read-model with the tags field but no story is downstream of s10 in the Epic's graph.

nonFunctional.performance: The list panel (s2) must not re-parse every on-disk pad file per render; sc3's read-model is served from the daemon's index instead. Backlink-query latency targets and the note-size cap for sc2's new daemon IPC are explicitly an open PRD decision (DEF §8) to resolve before s2/s5/s6 build. Avoid full reparses/echo loops on selection updates; set a supported note-size/performance budget in S001 LLD.
nonFunctional.security: The home-dir scratchpad store stays outside repo enrollment per k4; the daemon's new index only joins validated target identity (sc1/sc2), never widening default document search or repo registration to the store itself. Bundle editor assets locally under CSP. Validate bridge actions, target URI and version; no arbitrary file paths, command dispatch or cloud calls from document content. Library AI features remain disabled. Native I/O follows accepted VS Code behavior; guarded store operations remain distinct.
nonFunctional.observability: Log identity/version and operation failures without note text. Surface unsupported syntax and synchronization errors while preserving original content/drafts. Distinguish fake tests from live host evidence.
nonFunctional.durability: sc1's stableId must survive rename/move/archive/restore (s7); the daemon index's reconciliation strategy against the home-dir store's actual file state (so it never serves a stale binding indefinitely) is a design.story decision. Never write/normalize merely by opening a file. Unknown syntax, custom links and diagram fences must round-trip or unsafe edits must be refused with the original preserved. Never silently overwrite newer revisions. Validate cross-window conflict, undo/redo, reload and recovery against normal VS Code behavior.

api.name: ScratchPanels
api.signature: interface ScratchPanels { openBrowse(): Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined>; openDocument(id: string): Promise<void>; refreshBrowse(): Promise<void>; deleteDocument(id: string): Promise<'deleted' | 'cancelled'>; dispose(): void; }

errors.condition: Editor open, synchronization or targeted tab operation fails.

preconditions: Every chat/browse event boundary attaches a rejection handler. Creation and open failure are reported separately; refresh failures do not suppress opening.

One per-TextDocument queue is shared by every pane in a window. Bind each message to its registered URI, random paneSessionId, monotonic draftSeq/editId and accepted baseVersion/digest; reject cross-document, stale-session, oversized, duplicate-conflicting and unknown messages.
postconditions: Synchronization: every local doc-changing transaction immediately reports its latest Markdown draft to the host, even while another edit is in flight; selection-only transactions report no edit. Host retains the latest draft for recovery, serializes one WorkspaceEdit at a time, and coalesces superseded queued snapshots. Before applying, recheck base version/digest. A queued descendant may advance only after its identified parent was acknowledged and no unrelated document edit intervened; otherwise reject and retain it as a recovery draft.

Compute a minimal contiguous text replacement from the accepted source to the admitted Markdown proposal; do not full-replace solely for convenience. Await workspace.applyEdit and acknowledge with draftSeq, document version/digest and canonical snapshot. Match self-origin onDidChange events to the in-flight proposal. Broadcast host/undo/external updates to all panes without echo. An acknowledgement for an older local sequence advances the base but must not overwrite a newer local draft. Any unmatched update freezes mutation and preserves the competing draft for explicit recovery, never last-writer-wins.

Keep a bounded per-document recovery record in extension-owned local storage for received but unapplied drafts, keyed by canonical URI and sequence, with 1 MiB text bound. Persist before acknowledging receipt; clear only when committed or explicitly discarded. A normal tab dispose must not cancel an already accepted document edit or delete its recovery record. On reopening, show pending recovery without silently overwriting the canonical document. Test close/reload while edits are in flight; if host lifecycle safety cannot be demonstrated, validation fails.

Single undo authority: remove the published Milkdown history plugin array via Editor.remove before create and replace its key/toolbar actions with host undo/redo commands for the intended document. Drain pending proposals and verify active target before invoking; host change broadcasts are authoritative, never added to another Milkdown history. Standard save command drains first. onWillSaveTextDocument is only a best-effort drain hook because VS Code can bypass it; normal save/autosave guarantees apply, and pending drafts remain recoverable rather than falsely marked saved.

Fidelity admission: opening, parsing, toggling lock or selecting never writes. Retain the original source. Before allowing a proposal, compare the configured Markdown parse/serialize/parse structure and required raw-syntax fingerprints, including front matter, HTML/comments, code/diagram fences and literal future link syntax. Unknown constructs need exact preservation through an explicitly tested opaque node/plugin; absent that, refuse mutation with the original/draft intact. A minimal diff is not a fidelity proof. Test that supported edits cannot drop unrelated unknown content; no best-effort destructive save.

Send: clicking captures immutable {paneSessionId,draftSeq,docVersion,selectedText} before focus changes. selectedText is plain selected content from the current ProseMirror document, preserving paragraph boundaries. Drain the captured draft sequence, validate source/session/version and cap with existing capUtf8 (65,536 bytes including ellipsis). If the source changed incompatibly, retain the captured text and report retry; never silently recapture different text. Then use the existing scratch-host send-to-chat route: reveal, await ready, check disposed, insert into composer. No submit, clipboard, attachment or model call.

Deletion: both chat and browse call deleteDocument. Serialize against local document edits, drain pending drafts and inspect all exact-URI text/custom tabs across groups. Dirty/pending/recovery state cancels and asks the user to save/revert; never force discard. Await targeted closure of clean matching tabs, cancel on false, recheck state and revalidate before deleteScratch. On unlink failure attempt to reopen the still-existing note and report failure. Cross-window global exclusion is not promised; native external-delete/conflict behavior must preserve other windows' dirty drafts.

Save notifications: activation owns one disposable onDidSaveTextDocument listener scoped to validated scratchpad URIs; coalesce refreshBrowse and proposed ScratchHost.refreshList. Catch each refresh separately, never open closed UI or turn a successful save into a failed save. Creation/deletion and fallback saves use the same refresh boundary.

Remove legacy documentBodyHtml/documentBootstrap, scratch-save/scratch-saved/scratch-dirty/readiness/content messages and associated types, callbacks, onDocMessage, replySaved, showingId, invalidateId and old generations in one change. Retain capUtf8, the browse webview, six chat intents and existing guarded store APIs. The new versioned editor bridge is a different typed protocol, not reuse of the retired save channel.

alternativesConsidered.name: Versioned minimal-edit bridge
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep TextDocument authoritative and send coalesced, versioned renderer proposals that become minimal text edits.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Milkdown maintains the transient rendered draft while the extension host serializes changes per TextDocument. Each pane has one in-flight proposal and coalesces later local changes. The host validates URI, pane session, base document version and content digest, derives a minimal contiguous text replacement against the accepted base, and uses WorkspaceEdit. Host snapshots acknowledge edits and synchronize all panes.

Only acknowledged state is canonical. Host updates never echo into new proposals. Independent Milkdown history is removed; explicit undo/redo drains the pending queue then invokes the host stack for the intended resource. Stale proposals preserve recovery drafts instead of overwriting new content. Rich editing is admitted only when the supported syntax round-trips without semantic/opaque-content loss.
pros: One authoritative document and host undo history; rejection behavior is explicit.
Limits document replacement scope and carries actual source/version identity for Send and synchronization.
cons: Requires protocol/session/edit IDs, acknowledgement ordering and failure recovery tests.
Minimal diff does not itself prove Markdown fidelity; serializer loss/unsupported syntax is separately guarded.

alternativesConsidered.name: Versioned whole-document checkpoint bridge
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Use the same authoritative TextDocument but apply an acknowledged full-buffer replacement per coalesced checkpoint.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
The renderer emits a full Markdown snapshot after a short coalescing interval. The host validates base version/digest and applies a whole-document WorkspaceEdit, then broadcasts authoritative state. Selection Send, lock control, input validation and syntax admission are identical to a1.

This reduces mapping logic but entire-buffer edits disturb ranges and undo granularity and can produce large replacements for small edits. It still cannot bypass stale-version rejection, fidelity checks or normal save/conflict behavior.
pros: Simpler snapshot mapping useful as a qualification baseline.
Retains canonical TextDocument authority and the same stale-edit guard.
cons: Large replacements for small changes and weaker range/undo behavior.
Same fidelity gate and synchronization lifecycle are still necessary.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: No benefit to ac2/ac3/ac4 or sc1; full replacements weaken ac1's document interaction behavior.

createScratchHost's onMessage is the primary driver of the functions this Story touches: case 'scratch-open' calls deps.panels.openDocument(msg.id) (line 150); case 'scratch-new' awaits deps.panels.openDocument(entry.id) and checks `if (opened === undefined) log.warn('...did not open')` (lines 137-138) — a check that depends on openDocument's current Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> return shape; case 'scratch-delete' calls deps.panels.invalidateId(msg.id) then deps.panels.closeDocumentIfShowing(msg.id) (lines 155,165); case 'scratch-browse' calls deps.panels.openBrowse() (line 171). case 'scratch-open-menu' (line 109) only calls sendScratchList() — it never calls openDocument and needs no change from this Story.
Activation supplies store and document send/save/dirty callbacks to createScratchPanels.
SP-5 retains existing Send to chat; SP-4 requires preserved committed data and drafts on failure/conflict.

User rejected clipboard/two views, requested embeddable JS Markdown libraries, checked Milkdown and said it looks good. Normal VS Code save behavior accepted; Send requires a click and only inserts into composer.

Crepe has a configurable floating selection toolbar; library controls and plugins are owned by the embedding application. Source confirms editable control and customizable tooltip; no integration/round-trip proof implied.
CustomTextEditorProvider renders an owned webview over a VS Code TextDocument; changes must synchronize to that document.
Approved DEF7; S001 single-pane Milkdown editor, remembered lock, explicit Send click.
Approved HLD5; shared sc1 ownership and sibling boundaries preserved.
Published 7.23.0 package metadata/types inspected without installing: Crepe.setReadonly, Editor.remove, history plugin array and image upload/display callbacks. Integration still untested.
Default formatting tooltip requires editable view; a separate owned selection Send tooltip is required.
